description: One entry per spreadsheet that scripts/sheet_io.py converts between XLSX (for people) and JSON (for scripts and agents). Columns, required cells and allowed values live here, not in code. `xlsx`, `json` and `audit` name constants in scripts/paths.py. A column with "in_json": false is kept in the spreadsheet only. `decision` says which side is the decision: spreadsheet (default) or json (the sheet is exported for review and its edits imported back). `shape` names a converter for a JSON that is not a flat list (mapping, questions: record_ai_bank.py).

ai_areas.json_description: AI areas of the AI RMF assessment: the ways AI is used and the components of the AI ecosystem, each with the attack areas it impacts. Generated from data/ai/authoring/ai_areas.xlsx by scripts/sheet_io.py import; the spreadsheet is the decision, edit it, not this file. Model: AI_RMF_Mapping_Sheet_Design.md.

columns.help: Short lowercase id, letters, digits and _ only. The intake menus use it; never reuse an id for a different area.
Plain name of the way AI is used, or of the part of the AI ecosystem.
usage: a way AI is used (or used around you). component: a part of the AI ecosystem.
Which question bank: consumer, producer or both.

The attack areas a failure here hits, one or more: data (exposed, leaked, poisoned), access (permissions and credentials used or abused), process (a business process or decision goes wrong), assets (model, code or infrastructure stolen, damaged or taken down), people (individuals harmed by what the AI says or decides: wrong advice, unfair treatment, safety; AI RMF harm to People). Ecosystem harm is not used.
What is exposed and what can go wrong. The agents that draft the mapping read this.
One question that shows the area, for people reading the sheet. Not copied to the JSON.

readme: AI areas of the AI RMF assessment: how AI is used (usage) and what the AI is made of (component), and which attack areas each one impacts.
This spreadsheet is the decision. Scripts never read it directly: after editing, run
.venv/bin/python ./scripts/sheet_io.py import ai_areas
which checks every row and writes data/ai/ai_areas.json. If anything is wrong it lists the problems and writes nothing.
The freshness check reports this sheet as stale until it has been imported.
Which areas a client gets comes from the intake: the usage and component menus list these ids, and data/ai/scope_rules.json (ai_area_rules) adds the automatic ones.
Each area is checked through MAP, MEASURE and MANAGE in the mapping step (GOVERN is the foundation, asked once for the organisation); see AI_RMF_Mapping_Sheet_Design.md.
Dropdowns limit Kind and Applies to; Impact takes one or more of data, access, process, assets, people separated by commas. Column help is below.

columns.help: Do not edit. The AI area id.
Do not edit. From ai_areas.json.
Do not edit. MAP (context), MEASURE (checking), MANAGE (responding). GOVERN is not here: it is the foundation, asked once for the organisation.
Do not edit. The AI RMF subcategory.
Do not edit. The Playbook's outcome for the subcategory.
yes: this subcategory checks this area (a row). no: it does not. Change it to add or remove a row.

Why for this area: one sentence on what this subcategory checks about this area (at least 20 characters). Needed when Mapped is yes. A cell note (hover) says when two subcategories were folded into one row: the folded one is asked and scored through that row.
Safeguard ids separated by commas (e.g. MCP-8.2, MCP-8.5), from the area's candidates (mapping_rules.json area_cis). May be empty.
Do not edit. The titles of the safeguards as exported; refreshed on the next export.
One or more of the area's impacts, separated by commas. Needed when Mapped is yes.

pass, or needs_human_review. On a Mapped = yes line: the evaluator failed the row; set pass once you have decided it. On a Mapped = no line: the evaluator says this row is missing; map it (Mapped = yes, fill the line, Status pass) or set pass to keep it unmapped.

Do not edit. Why the evaluator failed the row, 'Missing:' when it says the row should exist, 'Note:' for a remark that does not block (e.g. the area's impacts look too narrow: change them in ai_areas.xlsx).
Do not edit. agent or human; a row you change becomes human on import.

Subcategories this row also covers (merged by the drafter): they are asked and scored through this row. Remove one to unfold it (it then has no row unless you map its own line); clear the cell before setting Mapped to no.

readme: The AI RMF mapping for review: one line per AI area x MAP, MEASURE or MANAGE subcategory, mapped or not.

Check the Mapped = yes lines (right or wrong?), then scan the Mapped = no lines for anything missing. Filter by AI area or by Subcategory. Filter Status = needs_human_review for what the evaluator flagged: failed rows, and Mapped = no lines it says are missing.
The Coverage sheet shows, per subcategory, which areas reach it; a subcategory no area reaches stands out there.
data/ai/mapping.json is the decision; this sheet is exported from it. After editing, run
.venv/bin/python ./scripts/sheet_io.py import mapping
which checks every area against data/ai/mapping_rules.json (candidate safeguards, impacts, required checks) and writes mapping.json. If anything is wrong it lists the problems and writes nothing.
A line you change (or a Status you set) is stored as decided_by human. Refresh the sheet after a new area is drafted with
.venv/bin/python ./scripts/sheet_io.py export mapping
which refuses to overwrite edits you have not imported.
The AI RMF area questions for review: one line per question. A question is scored on its subcategory and asked for the areas it covers.
Filter by Subcategory or Areas covered; filter Status = needs_human_review for what the evaluator still failed.
data/ai/banks/question_bank_ai_rmf_areas.json is the decision; this sheet is exported from it. After editing, run
.venv/bin/python ./scripts/sheet_io.py import area_questions

which checks the whole bank with the same rules as recording (every area's row asked once or twice per role its area allows; roles the areas allow; safeguards of the rows; folded subcategories cited) and writes the bank. If anything is wrong it lists the problems and writes nothing.
A subcategory you change (or whose Status you set) is stored as decided_by human; a later generator run does not overwrite it unless asked to.
Refresh the sheet after questions are recorded with
.venv/bin/python ./scripts/sheet_io.py export area_questions
which refuses to overwrite edits you have not imported.

columns.help: Do not edit. The AI RMF subcategory the question is scored on.
Do not edit. The Playbook's outcome for the subcategory.
Do not edit. The question's number within its subcategory, as exported. Leave blank on a line you add for a new question; delete a line to remove its question.

AI area ids the question is asked for, separated by commas (e.g. agent, mcp_tools); each must have a mapping row on this subcategory. Several areas: one shared question, shown to the client with 'This question covers: ...' naming only the client's areas, so the text must not name an area.
Do not edit. The names of the areas covered, as exported.

Who gets the question, separated by commas: consumer (uses AI built by others), producer (builds or tunes its own model), none (says it uses no AI; only AI policy and shadow-AI questions). consumer, producer = both. An area question may carry only roles its areas allow (none only on invisible_usage).
Only for a question asked of producers alone: built_on_existing_model (base-model questions) or given_to_others (release questions). The question is then asked only of producers with that answer.
The question as the client reads it. Practice-revealing (how, who, how often, what evidence), never yes / no.
The Playbook suggested actions the question is grounded in, separated by commas, e.g. 'MEASURE 2.8 — suggested action 4'.
Safeguard ids the question cites as evidence, separated by commas; only safeguards of the rows it covers.
pass, or needs_human_review (the evaluator still failed this question, or the whole subcategory). Set pass once you have decided; a subcategory is pass only when all its lines are.
Do not edit. Why the evaluator failed this question; 'Whole subcategory:' is a failure of the subcategory as a whole (something no question asks), shown on each of its lines.
Do not edit. agent, or human once you changed the subcategory in this sheet.

readme: The AI RMF foundation questions for review: one line per question, asked once for the whole organisation (GOVERN and the 12 foundation subcategories).
Filter Status = needs_human_review for what the evaluator still failed.
data/ai/banks/question_bank_ai_rmf_foundation.json is the decision; this sheet is exported from it. After editing, run
.venv/bin/python ./scripts/sheet_io.py import foundation_questions

which checks the whole bank with the same rules as recording (1 to 4 questions per subcategory plus one asked of producers only, at least one consumer and one producer question without a producer flag, no safeguards) and writes the bank. If anything is wrong it lists the problems and writes nothing.
A subcategory you change (or whose Status you set) is stored as decided_by human; a later generator run does not overwrite it unless asked to.
Refresh the sheet after questions are recorded with
.venv/bin/python ./scripts/sheet_io.py export foundation_questions
which refuses to overwrite edits you have not imported.
